newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS - Brazilians attack USDA coffee crop forecast.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Brazilians attack USDA coffee crop forecast.

text.p: Confusion this afternoon over the current U.S. Department of Agriculture's estimate of the 1996/97 Brazilian coffee crop has undermined the agency's credibility in crop forecasting, Brazilian traders said.
"The last mark of credibility for some people in crop forecasting is going down the drain," said Francisco Ourique, director of Flavour Coffee.
"Now everyone is the world is going to have two crop figures in mind as far as the USDA is concerned," he added.

Earlier on Friday the text of a semi-annual report written by a U.S. agricultural attache in Sao Paulo and dated Nov 5 was released by USDA in Washington, containing an estimate for the 1996/97 crop of 25.8 million bags, "a decrease of over six percent from the previous estimate," it said.

But USDA on Dec 13 in its world coffee production production forecast officially pegged 1996/97 Brazilian output at 27 million bags, a figure which USDA analyst Edmond Missiaen repeated this afternoon was the official forecast.
The attache's text caused New York futures to rally before the market pulled back on the USDA's subsequent clarification.
Missiaen said USDA had used the attache report from the field as only one factor in its official production estimates.
"In fact, if you talked to the attache now, he's using the 27 (million bag estimate). We talk to the attache before we make a major change from what he or she reports," he said.
Late on Friday USDA confirmed the 27 million bag Brazilian estimate in its latest world supply-demand report.

But traders in Brazil said they believe the discrepancy reflects a change in staff this year when the USDA decided to close down the Foreign Agricultural Service office in Rio de Janeiro, previously responsible for surveys of Brazil coffee.
The man responsible was Leon Yallouz, who worked for USDA for 37 years and visited Brazil coffee plantations 144 times.
Yallouz now works as as a consultant and his estimate of the 1997/98 crop for private clients is expected to set the pace for other expectations of the coming crop.
Yallouz said that he had not seen any revisions to the USDA estimate but added that "in my personal opinion, the 1996/97 crop is a minimum of 27 million bags".
"In reality the 1996/97 figure is not such an issue to the market. What is important is Yallouz's 1997/98 figure," said Jair Coser, president of leading exporter Unicafe.
"All this is really too much like Carnival," said John Wolthers of Santos export firm Icatu/Sumatra.
